how have you been? phrase

also how’ve you been?, have you been well?, have you been keeping well?

classical

Plaut. Trin. 50: Valēn'? valuistīn'?
Plaut. Curc. 16: salvē, valuistīn'?
Plaut. Epid. 1.1.15: perpetuōn' valuistī? (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō)
Traupman 18: hello, how’ve you been?, salvē, valuistīne?

Valuistīne?

question: perfect of valeō with -ne

have you been well?

Latin asks in the perfect, “have you been well?”, and the answer repeats the verb: Valuī. Spoken, the question is clipped to valuistīn'.

Examples

  • Valēn'? valuistīn'? — Valeō, et valuī rēctius.

    Are you well? Have you been well? — I am, and I’ve been better.Plaut. Trin. 50–50b

  • salvē, valuistīn'?

    hello, have you been well?Plaut. Curc. 16

  • Salvē. Valuistīne?

    Hello. How’ve you been?Traupman 18

See also how are you?, I’m fine, hello, is it …?.
